##### 4. Automated AST Directory Sweeper Buzzer

`packages/299.lore/00.lore.unit/buz/hygieneSentinel.buzz.ts`:

```typescript
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

export interface HygieneSentinelReport {
  totalFilesScanned: number
  hasSrcDirectory: boolean
  debuggerViolations: { file: string; line: number; text: string }[]
  nonAsciiViolations: { file: string; line: number; text: string }[]
  deadCodeViolations: { file: string; token: string }[]
  isClean: boolean
}

function sweepDirectory(dir: string, fileList: string[] = []): string[] {
  const entries = fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })
  for (const entry of entries) {
    if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === 'dist' || entry.name === '.git') {
      continue
    }
    const fullPath = path.join(dir, entry.name)
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      sweepDirectory(fullPath, fileList)
    } else if (entry.isFile() && (entry.name.endsWith('.ts') || entry.name.endsWith('.tsx'))) {
      fileList.push(fullPath)
    }
  }
  return fileList
}

export function runHygieneSentinelSweep(packageRoot: string): HygieneSentinelReport {
  const srcDir = path.join(packageRoot, 'src')
  const hasSrcDirectory = fs.existsSync(srcDir)
  const tsFiles = sweepDirectory(packageRoot)
  
  const debuggerViolations: { file: string; line: number; text: string }[] = []
  const nonAsciiViolations: { file: string; line: number; text: string }[] = []
  const deadCodeViolations: { file: string; token: string }[] = []

  const debuggerRegex = /\bdebugger\b/
  const nonAsciiRegex = /[\x80-\xFF\u{1F300}-\u{1FAD6}]/u

  for (const filePath of tsFiles) {
    const relPath = path.relative(packageRoot, filePath).replace(/\\/g, '/')
    const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')
    const lines = content.split('\n')

    lines.forEach((line, idx) => {
      if (debuggerRegex.test(line)) {
        debuggerViolations.push({ file: relPath, line: idx + 1, text: line.trim() })
      }
      if (nonAsciiRegex.test(line)) {
        nonAsciiViolations.push({ file: relPath, line: idx + 1, text: line.trim() })
      }
    })

    if (relPath === '00.lore.unit/buz/lore.buzz.ts') {
      if (content.includes('lore.list()')) {
        deadCodeViolations.push({ file: relPath, token: 'lore.list()' })
      }
      if (content.includes('zero00-lore.onrender.com')) {
        deadCodeViolations.push({ file: relPath, token: 'zero00-lore.onrender.com' })
      }
    }
  }

  const isClean =
    !hasSrcDirectory &&
    debuggerViolations.length === 0 &&
    nonAsciiViolations.length === 0 &&
    deadCodeViolations.length === 0

  return {
    totalFilesScanned: tsFiles.length,
    hasSrcDirectory,
    debuggerViolations,
    nonAsciiViolations,
    deadCodeViolations,
    isClean,
  }
}
```

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod'

export const RuleCategoryEnum = z.enum([
  'PHYSICAL',
  'SOMATIC',
  'EPISTEMIC',
  'SOCIAL',
  'LOGISTICAL',
])
export type RuleCategory = z.infer<typeof RuleCategoryEnum>

export const RuleSeverityClassEnum = z.enum([
  'TIER_1_HARD_INVARIANT',
  'TIER_2_AUDITED_ONTOLOGY',
  'TIER_3_SOFT_STYLOMETRIC',
])
export type RuleSeverityClass = z.infer<typeof RuleSeverityClassEnum>

export const RuleSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().regex(/^rule_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[RULE_SCHEMA_BREACH] id must match pattern ^rule_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    category: RuleCategoryEnum,
    severity_class: RuleSeverityClassEnum,
    description: z.string().min(10, {
      message: '[RULE_SCHEMA_BREACH] description must be at least 10 characters',
    }),
    pardonable: z.boolean().default(false),
    max_tolerated_pardon_frequency_bps: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] max_tolerated_pardon_frequency_bps must be an integer' })
      .min(0, { message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] frequency cannot be negative' })
      .max(10000, { message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] frequency cannot exceed 10000 basis points' })
      .default(0),
    owning_entity_types: z
      .array(z.enum(['character', 'location', 'possession', 'grievance', 'scene']))
      .min(1, { message: '[RULE_SCHEMA_BREACH] owning_entity_types must not be empty' }),
  })
  .strict()
  .refine(
    (rule) => {
      const isHardInvariant = ['PHYSICAL', 'SOMATIC', 'EPISTEMIC'].includes(rule.category)
      if (isHardInvariant && rule.pardonable === true) {
        return false
      }
      return true
    },
    {
      message: '[UNPARDONABLE_INVARIANT_BREACH] PHYSICAL, SOMATIC, and EPISTEMIC rules must declare pardonable: false',
      path: ['pardonable'],
    },
  )

export type Rule = z.infer<typeof RuleSchema>

export const AuthorizerRoleEnum = z.enum([
  'LEAD_ARCHITECT',
  'SHOWRUNNER',
  'SCENE_DIRECTOR',
  'SYSTEM_ADMIN',
])
export type AuthorizerRole = z.infer<typeof AuthorizerRoleEnum>

export const AuthorizerSchema = z
  .object({
    id: z.string().regex(/^auth_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[AUTH_SCHEMA_BREACH] id must match pattern ^auth_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    name: z.string().min(1, { message: '[AUTH_SCHEMA_BREACH] name is required' }),
    role: AuthorizerRoleEnum,
    permitted_categories: z
      .array(RuleCategoryEnum)
      .min(1, { message: '[AUTH_SCHEMA_BREACH] permitted_categories must not be empty' }),
  })
  .strict()

export type Authorizer = z.infer<typeof AuthorizerSchema>
```

###### 2. Create: `packages/299.lore/03.laws.unit/fce/pardon.schema.ts`

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod'

export const SomaticMutationPayloadSchema = z
  .object({
    condition_added: z.string().min(1).optional(),
    temporary_motor_mask_relief: z.string().min(1).optional(),
    exhaustion_increment_bps: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] exhaustion_increment_bps must be integer' })
      .min(0)
      .max(10000)
      .optional(),
  })
  .strict()

export const LogisticalMutationPayloadSchema = z
  .object({
    capacity_override_grams: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] capacity_override_grams must be integer' })
      .min(0)
      .optional(),
    slot_borrow: z
      .object({
        source_slot: z.enum(['worn', 'held', 'carried', 'cached']),
        target_slot: z.enum(['worn', 'held', 'carried', 'cached']),
      })
      .strict()
      .optional(),
  })
  .strict()

export const SocialMutationPayloadSchema = z
  .object({
    temporary_leverage_delta_bps: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] temporary_leverage_delta_bps must be integer' })
      .optional(),
    deflection_target_override: z.string().regex(/^char_[a-z0-9_]+$/).optional(),
  })
  .strict()

export const InjectedStateMutationSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('vector', [
  z.object({
    vector: z.literal('somatic'),
    payload: SomaticMutationPayloadSchema,
  }),
  z.object({
    vector: z.literal('logistical'),
    payload: LogisticalMutationPayloadSchema,
  }),
  z.object({
    vector: z.literal('social'),
    payload: SocialMutationPayloadSchema,
  }),
])
export type InjectedStateMutation = z.infer<typeof InjectedStateMutationSchema>

export const PardonScopeSchema = z
  .object({
    series_slug: z.string().min(1),
    episode_id: z.string().min(1),
    scene_id: z.string().min(1),
    shot_id: z.string().optional(),
    entity_id: z.string().regex(/^char_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[PARDON_SCHEMA_BREACH] entity_id must match character identifier',
    }),
  })
  .strict()
export type PardonScope = z.infer<typeof PardonScopeSchema>

export const PardonRecordSchema = z
  .object({
    pardon_id: z.string().regex(/^pardon_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[PARDON_SCHEMA_BREACH] pardon_id must match pattern ^pardon_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    target: PardonScopeSchema,
    rule_id: z.string().regex(/^rule_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[PARDON_SCHEMA_BREACH] rule_id must match pattern ^rule_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    authorizer_id: z.string().regex(/^auth_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[PARDON_SCHEMA_BREACH] authorizer_id must match pattern ^auth_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    justification: z.string().min(20, {
      message: '[PARDON_JUSTIFICATION_TOO_SHORT] minimum 20 characters required for principled audit review',
    }),
    granted_against_canon_hash: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, {
      message: '[INVALID_CANON_HASH] granted_against_canon_hash must be a 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal string',
    }),
    injected_state_mutation: InjectedStateMutationSchema.optional(),
    granted_at_epoch: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] granted_at_epoch must be integer' })
      .nonnegative()
      .default(0),
  })
  .strict()

export type PardonRecord = z.infer<typeof PardonRecordSchema>
```

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
import {

describe('03.laws.unit :: Constitutional Rule Registry & Pardon Schema', () => {
  it('validates a compliant unpardonable physical rule', () => {
    const candidate = {
      id: 'rule_kinetic_limb_conservation',
      category: 'PHYSICAL',
      severity_class: 'TIER_1_HARD_INVARIANT',
      description: 'Characters cannot execute physical actions requiring severed limbs.',
      pardonable: false,
      max_tolerated_pardon_frequency_bps: 0,
      owning_entity_types: ['character'],
    }
    const result = RuleSchema.safeParse(candidate)
    expect(result.success).toBe(true)
  })

  it('rejects self-contradictory rules declaring PHYSICAL with pardonable: true', () => {
    const illegal = {
      id: 'rule_kinetic_limb_conservation',
      category: 'PHYSICAL',
      severity_class: 'TIER_1_HARD_INVARIANT',
      description: 'Illegal physical rule waiver.',
      pardonable: true,
      max_tolerated_pardon_frequency_bps: 100,
      owning_entity_types: ['character'],
    }
    const result = RuleSchema.safeParse(illegal)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[UNPARDONABLE_INVARIANT_BREACH]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects self-contradictory rules declaring SOMATIC with pardonable: true', () => {
    const illegal = {
```

#### **User Story**

In the subterranean editorial cabin, the lead narrative architect stares at the series bible. For three seasons, the unbending physical laws of *Under the Floorboards* have given the story its claustrophobic, visceral weight: tallow burns at a fixed rate, severed limbs cannot grip levers, and cold drafts through iron grates carry sound across exact acoustic decibels. But pressure is mounting from a guest director who wants a one-armed character to magically wield a two-handed industrial wrench for a dramatic shot, claiming an arbitrary "director's waiver."

In legacy pipelines, that single compromise would have slipped into production as a loose note, quietly breaking canon continuity and shattering the show's somatic integrity. But here, the architect does not have to argue or play gatekeeper through human exhaustion. The engine itself enforces constitutional governance.

The architect watches as the director attempts to register the waiver. The compiler halts before burning a single dollar of rendering compute: `[UNPARDONABLE_INVARIANT_BREACH] PHYSICAL, SOMATIC, and EPISTEMIC rules must declare pardonable: false`. The rule itself dictates authority, not the requester. Only audited logistical borrowings and social leverages can be granted dispensations, and only by authorized showrunners holding cryptographic provenance. The lead architect smiles, leans back from the terminal, and breathes easy: the reality of the world remains unbroken.

#### 2. Create: `packages/299.lore/03.laws.unit/buz/pardon.buzz.ts`

```typescript
import type { Rule, Authorizer } from '../fce/rule.schema.js'
import type { PardonRecord } from '../fce/pardon.schema.js'
import type {
  PardonDiagnostic,
  PardonValidationResult,
} from '../fce/pardonValidation.bit.js'
import type { LawsModel } from '../laws.model.js'
import type PardonEvaluatorBit from '../fce/pardonValidation.bit.js'
import type State from '../../99.core/state.js'

export function validatePass2Pardons(
  pardons: Map<string, PardonRecord> | Record<string, PardonRecord>,
  rules: Map<string, Rule>,
  authorizers: Map<string, Authorizer>,
  entities: {
    characters?: Record<string, any>
    locations?: Record<string, any>
    possessions?: Record<string, any>
    grievances?: Record<string, any>
  },
  currentCanonHash: string,
  strictFrequencyAudit: boolean = false,
): PardonValidationResult {
  const errors: string[] = []
  const warnings: string[] = []
  const appliedPardons: PardonRecord[] = []
  const usageCounts = new Map<string, number>()

  const pardonList: PardonRecord[] =
    pardons instanceof Map
      ? Array.from(pardons.values())
      : Object.values(pardons)

  for (const pardon of pardonList) {
    const pardonId = pardon.pardon_id

    // 1. Foreign-Key Existence of Target Entity
    const targetEntityId = pardon.target.entity_id
    const charExists = entities.characters && entities.characters[targetEntityId]
    const locExists = entities.locations && entities.locations[targetEntityId]
    const itemExists = entities.possessions && entities.possessions[targetEntityId]
    const grvExists = entities.grievances && entities.grievances[targetEntityId]

    if (!charExists && !locExists && !itemExists && !grvExists) {
      errors.push(
        `[PASS 2 PARDON ERROR] Pardon '${pardonId}' references non-existent target entity: '${targetEntityId}'`,
      )
    }

    // 2. Foreign-Key Existence of Rule ID
    const rule = rules.get(pardon.rule_id)
    if (!rule) {
      errors.push(
        `[PASS 2 PARDON ERROR] Pardon '${pardonId}' references unknown rule_id: '${pardon.rule_id}'`,
      )
      continue
    }

    // 3. Relational Authority Enforcement: Check Rule Pardonability
    if (rule.pardonable !== true) {
      errors.push(
        `[PASS 2 PARDON FATAL] Illegal waiver attempted! Rule '${rule.id}' carries category '${rule.category}' ` +
          `and is marked pardonable: false. Hard physical, somatic, and epistemic laws cannot be bypassed via pardons.`,
      )
    }

    // 4. Authorizer Existence and Category Scope Permissions
    const authorizer = authorizers.get(pardon.authorizer_id)
    if (!authorizer) {
      errors.push(
        `[PASS 2 PARDON ERROR] Unknown authorizer '${pardon.authorizer_id}' on pardon '${pardonId}'.`,
      )
    } else if (!authorizer.permitted_categories.includes(rule.category)) {
      errors.push(
        `[PASS 2 PARDON PERMISSION DENIED] Authorizer '${authorizer.name}' (${authorizer.role}) ` +
          `is not permitted to waive rules of category '${rule.category}'.`,
      )
    }

    // 5. Stale Canon Hash Guard
    if (pardon.granted_against_canon_hash !== currentCanonHash) {
      warnings.push(
        `>> [PARDON WARNING] Pardon '${pardonId}' was granted against canon hash ` +
          `'${pardon.granted_against_canon_hash.slice(0, 8)}...', but current hash is ` +
          `'${currentCanonHash.slice(0, 8)}...'. Re-ratification recommended.`,
      )
    }

    usageCounts.set(pardon.rule_id, (usageCounts.get(pardon.rule_id) || 0) + 1)
    appliedPardons.push(pardon)
  }

  // 6. Active Pardon Frequency Auditing
  for (const [ruleId, count] of usageCounts.entries()) {
    const rule = rules.get(ruleId)
    const limit = rule ? rule.max_tolerated_pardon_frequency_bps : 0
    if (rule && limit > 0 && count > limit) {
      const freqMsg =
        `[PASS 2 PARDON FREQUENCY BREACH] Rule '${ruleId}' permits at most ` +
        `${limit} active waivers, but ${count} are registered.`
      if (strictFrequencyAudit) {
        errors.push(freqMsg)
      } else {
        warnings.push(`>> [PARDON FREQUENCY ALERT] ${freqMsg}`)
      }
    }
  }

  return {
    valid: errors.length === 0,
    errors,
    warnings,
    appliedPardons,
  }
}

export const evaluatePardonWaivers = (
  cpy: LawsModel,
  bal: PardonEvaluatorBit,
  ste?: State,
): LawsModel => {
  const dat = bal?.dat
  if (!dat) {
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        lawBit: {
          idx: 'evaluate-pardon-waivers-err',
          val: -1,
          dat: { valid: false, errors: ['[MISSING_PAYLOAD] dat is required'], warnings: [], appliedPardons: [] },
        },
      })
    }
    return cpy
  }

  const result = validatePass2Pardons(
    dat.pardons,
    cpy.rules,
    cpy.authorizers,
    {},
    dat.currentCanonHash,
    dat.strictFrequencyAudit ?? false,
  )

  if (bal?.slv) {
    bal.slv({
      lawBit: {
        idx: 'evaluate-pardon-waivers',
        val: result.valid ? 0 : -1,
        dat: result,
      },
    })
  }
  return cpy
}
```

```typescript
import type { Action } from '../99.core/interface/action.interface.js'
import type LawsBit from './fce/laws.bit.js'

  constructor(public bale: LawsBit) {}

export class EvaluatePardonWaivers implements Action {
  readonly type = EVALUATE_PARDON_WAIVERS
```

#### 4. Update: `packages/299.lore/03.laws.unit/laws.reduce.ts`

```typescript
import clone from 'clone-deep'
import * as Act from './laws.action.js'
import { LawsModel } from './laws.model.js'
import * as Buzz from './laws.buzzer.js'
import type State from '../99.core/state.js'

export function reducer(
  model: LawsModel = new LawsModel(),
  act: Act.Actions,
  state?: State,
): LawsModel {
  switch (act.type) {
    case Act.INIT_LAWS:
      return Buzz.initLaws(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.UPDATE_LAWS:
      return Buzz.updateLaws(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.EVALUATE_PARDON_WAIVERS:
      return Buzz.evaluatePardonWaivers(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    default:
      return model
  }
}
```

### **FUNCTIONAL MANDATE**

#### **User Story**

Deep in the production cycles of *Under the Floorboards*, the production bullpen is buzzing with eleventh-hour tension. A guest director and a storyboard artist are trying to solve an intense dramatic impasse: a character with an amputated left arm, trapped in a rising culvert siphon, needs to haul a fifty-pound brass pressure valve while gripping a rusted handrail. Under normal narrative friction, this action is a biological impossibility. In desperate haste, an ad-hoc waiver file is submitted into the episode bundle, signed with a hand-wavy note attempting to pardon the physical contradiction for dramatic effect.

Without an automated constitutional arbiter, that broken premise would leak straight into vocal synthesis, animation rigging, and timeline mastering, spawning downstream continuity anomalies across five subsequent episodes.

Instead, the moment the episode ingress pipeline triggers Pass 2 relational compilation, the **Fail-Closed Pardon Waiver Evaluator** intercepts the transaction. It does not politely warn or ask for confirmation. The engine inspects the targeted rule—`rule_bimanual_lift`—and immediately spots the hard invariant flag: `pardonable: false`. The compiler drops an iron curtain: `[PASS 2 PARDON FATAL] Illegal waiver attempted! Rule 'rule_bimanual_lift' carries category 'PHYSICAL' and is marked pardonable: false`.

The showrunner glances at the red telemetry receipt on console `cns00`. There is no debate, no political pressure, and no budget wasted rendering an impossible frame. The engine held the world together before compute was ever dispatched.

#### **Strategic Goal**

Supports the primary project objective of **Zero-Cost Compile-Time Invariance and Non-Negotiable World Physics ($T_0 = \$0.00$)**. By evaluating all declared exemptions during Pass 2 against strict rule category boundaries and authorizer signing permissions, this task guarantees that impossible physical actions, somatic limb violations, and protected epistemic secret leaks are caught and halted before downstream media synthesis engines are engaged.

#### **Context and Value**

- **The Strategic Value:** Eliminates the "Self-Declared Exemption Fallacy". Authority resides immutable on the **Rule**, never on the pardon petition. Guarantees that only flexible logistical borrowings or social status compromises can be waived, while foundational physical, biological, and epistemic invariants remain completely inviolable across transmedia production.
- **The Technical Challenge:** Validating multi-variable relational predicates in local memory—cross-referencing target entity existence, rule pardonability flags, authorizer permission scopes, integer basis-point frequency ceilings, and 64-character SHA-256 historical hash alignment—without floating-point errors, external network calls, or mutating the immutable harness boundary in `apps/995.library/`.

#### **Interface**

- **`000.goblin-lore` (`packages/299.lore` / `03.laws.unit`):** Self repository and home unit hosting the relational waiver evaluation engine, action bindings, and validation interfaces.
- **`43.compile.unit` (`packages/299.lore`):** Compiler harness that invokes `validatePass2Pardons` during `pass2Traverse` to halt candidate compilations if unauthorized or unpardonable waivers are detected.
- **`26.schema.unit` (`packages/299.lore`):** Supplies canonical entity structures, Somatic SAT constraints, and closed-world schema routing standards.
- **`apps/995.library` (`@camp_candor/995.library`):** Blessed terminal host runtime that invokes the waiver audit action via `run.ts` while enforcing strict boundary immutability (0 dirty lines).

```typescript
import fs from 'node:fs'

import type { CompileModel } from '../compile.model.js'
import type CompileBit from '../fce/compile.bit.js'
import type { CompileValidationReport } from '../fce/compile.bit.js'
import type State from '../../99.core/state.js'
import { validatePass2Pardons } from '../../03.laws.unit/buz/pardon.buzz.js'
import { CANONICAL_RULES, CANONICAL_AUTHORIZERS } from '../../03.laws.unit/fce/rule.schema.js'
import type { PardonRecord } from '../../03.laws.unit/fce/pardon.schema.js'

export {
  initCompile,
  runCompile,
  pass1Evaluate,
  offlineDeletionTest,
  stylometricLint,
  scaleBasisPoints,
  gate0Verify,

// Helper to resolve series pardons from disk
export function loadSeriesPardons(seriesDir: string): Map<string, PardonRecord> {
  const pardonsMap = new Map<string, PardonRecord>()
  const pardonsJsonPath = path.join(seriesDir, 'world', 'pardons.json')
  const pardonsDirPath = path.join(seriesDir, 'world', 'pardons')

  if (fs.existsSync(pardonsJsonPath)) {
    try {
      const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(pardonsJsonPath, 'utf8'))
      const list = Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : raw.records || []
      for (const p of list) {
        pardonsMap.set(p.pardon_id, p)
      }
    } catch {
      // Ignored here; caught by schema validators if corrupted
    }
  }

  if (fs.existsSync(pardonsDirPath)) {
    const files = fs.readdirSync(pardonsDirPath).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))
    for (const file of files) {
      try {
        const p = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(pardonsDirPath, file), 'utf8'))
        pardonsMap.set(p.pardon_id, p)
      } catch {
        // Handled in report
      }
    }
  }

  return pardonsMap
}

export const pass2Traverse = (
  cpy: CompileModel,
  bal: CompileBit,
  ste?: State,
): CompileModel => {
  cpy.status = 'PASS_2_TOPOLOGY'
  const seriesSlug = bal.seriesSlug || cpy.activeSeries || 'under-the-floorboards'
  const repoRoot = resolveRepoRoot()
  const seriesDir = path.join(repoRoot, 'series', seriesSlug)

  const report: CompileValidationReport = cpy.lastReport || {
    byte0Compliant: true,
    ascii7BitCompliant: true,
    schemaValid: true,
    somaticSatValid: true,
    foreignKeysValid: true,
    grievanceDagAcyclic: true,
    spatialPortalsReciprocal: true,
    acousticAttenuationValid: true,
    pardonsValid: true,
    appliedPardonsCount: 0,
    appliedPardons: [],
    errors: [],
    warnings: [],
  }

  // --- EXISTING PASS 2 LOGIC (Foreign keys, Grievance DAG, Portals) ---
  // ... (perform standard checks on cpy.entityCatalog)

  // --- PASS 2 PARDON WAIVER INTERCEPTOR ---
  const rulesMap = new Map(CANONICAL_RULES.map((r) => [r.id, r]))
  const authMap = new Map(CANONICAL_AUTHORIZERS.map((a) => [a.id, a]))
  const declaredPardons = loadSeriesPardons(seriesDir)

  const currentAnchorHash = cpy.lastMerkleHash || '0'.repeat(64)
  const pardonAudit = validatePass2Pardons(
    declaredPardons,
    rulesMap,
    authMap,
    cpy.entityCatalog || {},
    currentAnchorHash,
    true, // strict frequency enforcement
  )

  if (!pardonAudit.valid) {
    report.pardonsValid = false
    report.foreignKeysValid = false
    for (const err of pardonAudit.errors) {
      report.errors.push(err)
    }
    cpy.status = 'FAILED'
  } else {
    report.pardonsValid = true
    report.appliedPardonsCount = pardonAudit.appliedPardons.length
    report.appliedPardons = pardonAudit.appliedPardons
  }

  for (const warn of pardonAudit.warnings) {
    report.warnings.push(warn)
  }

  cpy.lastReport = report

  if (bal.slv) {
    bal.slv({
      cmpBit: {
        idx: 'pass2-traverse',
        val: report.errors.length === 0 ? 1 : 0,
        dat: { validationReport: report },
      },
    })
  }
  return cpy
}

export const pass3Seal = (
  cpy: CompileModel,
  bal: CompileBit,
  ste?: State,
): CompileModel => {
  cpy.status = 'PASS_3_SEALING'
  const seriesSlug = bal.seriesSlug || cpy.activeSeries || 'under-the-floorboards'
  const repoRoot = resolveRepoRoot()
  const compiledDir = path.join(repoRoot, 'compiled', seriesSlug)
  fs.mkdirSync(compiledDir, { recursive: true })

  const preSealEntities = cpy.entityCatalog || {}
  const appliedPardons = cpy.lastReport?.appliedPardons || []

  // Construct Canonical Pre-Seal Structure with Embedded Verified Pardons
  const preSealPayload = {
    schema_version: '1.0.0',
    series_slug: seriesSlug,
    _meta: {
      applied_pardons: appliedPardons,
    },
    catalog_summary: cpy.lastReport?.appliedPardonsCount !== undefined ? {
      ...summarizeCatalog(preSealEntities),
      pardonsCount: appliedPardons.length,
    } : summarizeCatalog(preSealEntities),
    entity_hashes: cpy.entityHashes || {},
    entities: preSealEntities,
  }

  const normalizedJcs = jcsSerialize(preSealPayload, true)
  const rootMerkleHash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(normalizedJcs, 'utf8').digest('hex')

  const sealedArtifact = {
    ...preSealPayload,
    root_merkle_hash: rootMerkleHash,
  }

  const biblePath = path.join(compiledDir, 'bible-state.json')
  fs.writeFileSync(biblePath, JSON.stringify(sealedArtifact, null, 2).normalize('NFC'), 'utf8')

  cpy.lastMerkleHash = rootMerkleHash
  cpy.status = 'SEALED'

  if (bal.slv) {
    bal.slv({
      cmpBit: {
        idx: 'pass3-seal',
        val: 1,
        rootMerkleHash,
        dat: { rootMerkleHash, biblePath },
      },
    })
  }
  return cpy
}
```

#### **User Story**

In the quiet of the late-night editorial suite, the lead continuity master initiates the nightly franchise compilation pass for *Under the Floorboards*. Earlier that afternoon, a remote scene director slipped an emergency waiver into the series world folder, attempting to excuse a one-armed boiler tender from the physical requirement of two-handed valves so that an impossible action sequence could be animated. In an undisciplined engine, such an exception would pass quietly through layout into synthesis, spawning broken character rigs, nonsensical dialogue, and expensive post-production cleanups.

Here, the legislative pipeline does not sleep. As the compiler traverses Pass 2, the **Pass Two Compiler Waiver Interceptor** sweeps the declared pardons and cross-references them against the constitutional ontology. The moment it detects that the waiver targets `rule_bimanual_lift`—a non-negotiable physical law declared `pardonable: false`—the compiler drops an iron shutter. It does not warn; it aborts. `cpy.status` transitions immediately to `FAILED`, the build freezes before generating a single audio packet or video frame, and console `cns00` streams an unambiguous error: `[PASS 2 PARDON FATAL] Illegal waiver attempted! Hard physical laws cannot be bypassed via pardons`.

Only when the scene is rewritten to respect biological reality does the compiler proceed to Pass 3. There, every legitimate logistical waiver granted by an authorized showrunner is immutably sealed into the Merkle tree's `_meta.applied_pardons`. The world's physical integrity remains absolute, and the canon's cryptographic provenance is preserved for all time.

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod'

export const ErrataClassificationEnum = z.enum([
  'FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION',
  'CHRONOLOGICAL_SLIP',
  'ANATOMICAL_ANOMALY',
  'ORTHOGRAPHIC_CANONIZATION',
  'HISTORICAL_RETCON',
])
export type ErrataClassification = z.infer<typeof ErrataClassificationEnum>

export const ErrataRecordSchema = z
  .object({
    errata_id: z.string().regex(/^err_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[ERRATA_SCHEMA_BREACH] errata_id must match pattern ^err_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    sequence_number: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] sequence_number must be an integer' })
      .min(1, { message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] sequence_number must be >= 1' }),
    classification: ErrataClassificationEnum,
    superseded_merkle_hash: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, {
      message: '[INVALID_HASH] superseded_merkle_hash must be a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 string',
    }),
    active_merkle_hash: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, {
      message: '[INVALID_HASH] active_merkle_hash must be a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 string',
    }),
    superseded_commit_sha: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/, {
      message: '[INVALID_COMMIT_SHA] superseded_commit_sha must be a 40-character lowercase hexadecimal Git SHA',
    }),
    active_commit_sha: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/, {
      message: '[INVALID_COMMIT_SHA] active_commit_sha must be a 40-character lowercase hexadecimal Git SHA',
    }),
    affected_entity_ids: z
      .array(z.string().min(1))
      .min(1, { message: '[ERRATA_EMPTY_TARGETS] at least one affected entity required' }),
    historical_episodes: z.array(z.string().min(1)).default([]),
    rationale: z.string().min(20, {
      message: '[RATIONALE_TOO_SHORT] rationale must contain at least 20 characters',
    }),
    recorded_at_epoch: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] recorded_at_epoch must be an integer' })
      .nonnegative({ message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] recorded_at_epoch cannot be negative' }),
  })
  .strict()

export type ErrataRecord = z.infer<typeof ErrataRecordSchema>

export const ErrataLedgerFileSchema = z
  .object({
    schema_version: z.literal('1.0.0'),
    series_slug: z.string().min(1),
    genesis_merkle_hash: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, {
      message: '[INVALID_HASH] genesis_merkle_hash must be a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 string',
    }),
    records: z.array(ErrataRecordSchema),
  })
  .strict()

export type ErrataLedgerFile = z.infer<typeof ErrataLedgerFileSchema>
```

```typescript
import {
  ErrataRecordSchema,
  ErrataLedgerFileSchema,
} from '../../03.laws.unit/fce/errata.schema.js'

export const VALIDATE_ERRATA_SCHEMA_LABEL = '[1] VALIDATE ERRATA RECORD SCHEMA'

export const validateErrataRecordSchemaAction = async (
  cpy: MenuModel,
  bal: MenuBit,
  ste?: State,
): Promise<MenuModel> => {
  await emitConsoleLine(ste, '>> [ERRATA:SCHEMA] Validating Errata Record Contract...')

  const validRecordCandidate = {
    errata_id: 'err_culvert_aperture_01',
    sequence_number: 1,
    classification: 'FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION',
    superseded_merkle_hash: '0'.repeat(64),
    active_merkle_hash: '1'.repeat(64),
    superseded_commit_sha: 'a'.repeat(40),
    active_commit_sha: 'b'.repeat(40),
    affected_entity_ids: ['loc_culvert_siphon'],
    historical_episodes: ['ep001'],
    rationale: 'Canonicalized culvert siphon pipe diameter to eight inches across series.',
    recorded_at_epoch: 100,
  }

  const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(validRecordCandidate)

  if (result.success) {
    await emitConsoleLine(
      ste,
      `>> [ERRATA:SCHEMA_OK] ErrataRecord ${validRecordCandidate.errata_id} validated. Status code: 0.`,
    )
    cpy.statusMessage = 'ERRATA_SCHEMA_VERIFIED'
  } else {
    for (const issue of result.error.issues) {
      await emitConsoleLine(ste, `:: [ERRATA:SCHEMA_FAIL] ${issue.message}`)
    }
    cpy.statusMessage = 'ERRATA_SCHEMA_BREACH'
  }

  if (bal.slv) {
    bal.slv({ mnuBit: { idx: 'validate-errata-schema', val: result.success ? 0 : -1, dat: result } })
  }
  return cpy
}
```

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
import {
  ErrataRecordSchema,
  ErrataLedgerFileSchema,
  ErrataClassificationEnum,
  type ErrataRecord,
  type ErrataLedgerFile,
} from '../fce/errata.schema.js'

describe('03.laws.unit :: Append-Only Errata Record Schema Contract', () => {
  const validSampleRecord: ErrataRecord = {
    errata_id: 'err_culvert_aperture_01',
    sequence_number: 1,
    classification: 'FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION',
    superseded_merkle_hash: 'a'.repeat(64),
    active_merkle_hash: 'b'.repeat(64),
    superseded_commit_sha: '1'.repeat(40),
    active_commit_sha: '2'.repeat(40),
    affected_entity_ids: ['loc_culvert_siphon'],
    historical_episodes: ['ep001'],
    rationale: 'Canonicalized culvert siphon pipe diameter to eight inches across series.',
    recorded_at_epoch: 100,
  }

  it('validates a compliant ErrataRecord payload', () => {
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(validSampleRecord)
    expect(result.success).toBe(true)
  })

  it('rejects floating-point numbers in sequence_number', () => {
    const floatSeq = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      sequence_number: 1.5,
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(floatSeq)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects sequence_number less than 1', () => {
    const zeroSeq = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      sequence_number: 0,
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(zeroSeq)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[OUT_OF_BOUNDS]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects floating-point numbers in recorded_at_epoch', () => {
    const floatEpoch = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      recorded_at_epoch: 100.25,
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(floatEpoch)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects rationales shorter than 20 characters', () => {
    const shortRationale = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      rationale: 'Too short',
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(shortRationale)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[RATIONALE_TOO_SHORT]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects non-hexadecimal or truncated superseded_merkle_hash', () => {
    const badHash = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      superseded_merkle_hash: 'not_a_valid_64_character_hex_hash',
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(badHash)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[INVALID_HASH]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects non-hexadecimal or truncated commit SHAs', () => {
    const badCommit = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      superseded_commit_sha: '12345',
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(badCommit)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[INVALID_COMMIT_SHA]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects empty affected_entity_ids array', () => {
    const emptyTargets = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      affected_entity_ids: [],
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(emptyTargets)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[ERRATA_EMPTY_TARGETS]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects undeclared properties in strict mode', () => {
    const rogueKeys = {
      ...validSampleRecord,
      unauthorized_flag: true,
    }
    const result = ErrataRecordSchema.safeParse(rogueKeys)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
  })

  it('validates a compliant ErrataLedgerFile payload', () => {
    const ledgerFile: ErrataLedgerFile = {
      schema_version: '1.0.0',
      series_slug: 'under-the-floorboards',
      genesis_merkle_hash: '0'.repeat(64),
      records: [validSampleRecord],
    }
    const result = ErrataLedgerFileSchema.safeParse(ledgerFile)
    expect(result.success).toBe(true)
  })
})
```

### **FUNCTIONAL MANDATE**

#### **User Story**

In the soundstage production suite, the master archivist reviews a pilot scene cut for *Under the Floorboards* where dialogue explicitly references a six-inch culvert drainage pipe. Three seasons later, during an intense escape sequence, tactical spatial geometry dictates that the culvert siphon aperture is eight inches wide to accommodate a character crawling with a tallow pack. In a traditional entertainment production pipeline, this discrepancy would result in a messy retroactive file edit: an intern would open the old scene file or Markdown dossier, quietly mutate the six into an eight, and overwrite the file on disk.

By doing so, historical integrity collapses. The original broadcast media hash breaks, cache keys become invalid, and downstream audio renderers can no longer differentiate between an authentic original release and an updated remaster.

With the **Append-Only Errata Record Schema**, the archivist never touches historical files. Instead, a formal `ErrataRecord` is drafted. The schema demands strict, mathematical rectitude: the record must be classified as a `FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION`, linked monotonically to `sequence_number: 1`, pinned to the exact `superseded_merkle_hash` of the original canon, and bound to the newly minted `active_merkle_hash` alongside a principled rationale of at least twenty characters. Un-schemaed property injections are rejected by strict closure, and floating-point timestamps are immediately trapped. Historical reality remains immutable, while the evolutionary lineage of the franchise is sealed in cryptographic amber.

#### **Strategic Goal**

Supports the primary project objective of **Zero-Cost Compile-Time Invariance & Non-Repudiable Historical Lineage ($T_0 = \$0.00$)**. By enforcing strict schema contracts over post-broadcast narrative corrections and retcons, this task guarantees that franchise state transitions can be audited as unbroken cryptographic hash chains, preserving historical media provenance without silent file mutations or retcon drift.

#### **Context & Value**

- **The Strategic Value:** Enables transmedia storyworlds to evolve across seasons and cycles without destroying the cryptographic ground truth of previously published episodes. Preserves media provenance by distinguishing immutable original broadcast replays from modern canonical remasters.
- **The Technical Challenge:** Designing a closed-world Zod schema (`ErrataRecordSchema` and `ErrataLedgerFileSchema`) that enforces strict hexadecimal string patterns for 64-character SHA-256 Merkle hashes and 40-character Git commit SHAs, eliminates floating-point drift on sequence numbers and epochs via integer gates, requires substantive rationale thresholds, and registers typed in-memory stores in `LawsModel` without illegal `src/` directories or runner harness modifications.

- **`000.goblin-lore` (`packages/299.lore` / `03.laws.unit`):** Self repository and home unit hosting the errata schemas, types, and in-memory `errataHistory` store in `LawsModel`.

```typescript
export function resolveRepoRoot(): string {
  let curr = process.cwd()
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    if (fs.existsSync(path.join(curr, 'series')) || fs.existsSync(path.join(curr, 'package.json'))) {
      if (fs.existsSync(path.join(curr, 'packages/299.lore'))) {

  return process.cwd()
}

export function loadErrataLedgerFile(ledgerPath: string, defaultGenesisHash?: string, seriesSlug?: string): ErrataLedgerFile {
  if (!fs.existsSync(ledgerPath)) {
    return {
      schema_version: '1.0.0',
      series_slug: seriesSlug || 'default-series',
      genesis_merkle_hash: defaultGenesisHash || '0'.repeat(64),
      records: [],
    }
  }

  const raw = fs.readFileSync(ledgerPath, 'utf8').trim()
  if (!raw) {
    return {
      schema_version: '1.0.0',
      series_slug: seriesSlug || 'default-series',
      genesis_merkle_hash: defaultGenesisHash || '0'.repeat(64),
      records: [],
    }
  }

  const parsed = JSON.parse(raw)
  return ErrataLedgerFileSchema.parse(parsed)
}

export function appendErrataRecord(
  seriesSlug: string,
  candidateRecord: ErrataRecord,
  customRepoRoot?: string,
): ErrataAppendResult {
  const validatedRecord = ErrataRecordSchema.parse(candidateRecord)
  const repoRoot = customRepoRoot || resolveRepoRoot()
  const worldDir = path.join(repoRoot, 'series', seriesSlug, 'world')
  const ledgerPath = path.join(worldDir, 'errata.json')

  if (!fs.existsSync(worldDir)) {
    fs.mkdirSync(worldDir, { recursive: true })
  }

  const ledger = loadErrataLedgerFile(ledgerPath, validatedRecord.superseded_merkle_hash, seriesSlug)
  const existingRecords = ledger.records

  // 1. Verify Monotonic Sequence Number Increment
  const expectedSeq = existingRecords.length + 1
  if (validatedRecord.sequence_number !== expectedSeq) {
    throw new Error(
      `[ERRATA_SEQUENCE_DISCONTINUITY] sequence_number must equal next index ${expectedSeq}, got ${validatedRecord.sequence_number}`,
    )
  }

  // 2. Reject Cyclic/No-Op Hashes
  if (validatedRecord.superseded_merkle_hash === validatedRecord.active_merkle_hash) {
    throw new Error(
      `[CYCLIC_HASH_REFERENCE] superseded_merkle_hash cannot equal active_merkle_hash (${validatedRecord.active_merkle_hash})`,
    )
  }

  // 3. Reject Duplicate Errata Identifiers
  if (existingRecords.some((r) => r.errata_id === validatedRecord.errata_id)) {
    throw new Error(
      `[DUPLICATE_ERRATA_ID] Errata entry with id '${validatedRecord.errata_id}' already exists in ledger`,
    )
  }

  // 4. Verify Cryptographic Lineage Chaining
  if (existingRecords.length === 0) {
    if (validatedRecord.superseded_merkle_hash !== ledger.genesis_merkle_hash) {
      throw new Error(
        `[GENESIS_HASH_MISMATCH] First errata record must supersede genesis hash '${ledger.genesis_merkle_hash}', got '${validatedRecord.superseded_merkle_hash}'`,
      )
    }
  } else {
    const tailRecord = existingRecords[existingRecords.length - 1]
    if (validatedRecord.superseded_merkle_hash !== tailRecord.active_merkle_hash) {
      throw new Error(
        `[HASH_DISCONTINUITY] superseded_merkle_hash '${validatedRecord.superseded_merkle_hash}' must match preceding tail active hash '${tailRecord.active_merkle_hash}'`,
      )
    }
  }

  // 5. Append and Write Atomically via Sibling Temporary File
  const updatedLedger: ErrataLedgerFile = {
    schema_version: '1.0.0',
    series_slug: seriesSlug,
    genesis_merkle_hash: ledger.genesis_merkle_hash,
    records: [...existingRecords, validatedRecord],
  }

  const tempUuid = crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex')
  const tempPath = path.join(worldDir, `.tmp_${tempUuid}_errata.json`)

  fs.writeFileSync(tempPath, JSON.stringify(updatedLedger, null, 2) + '\n', 'utf8')
  fs.renameSync(tempPath, ledgerPath)

  return {
    success: true,
    record: validatedRecord,
    ledgerPath,
    totalRecords: updatedLedger.records.length,
  }
}

export function verifyErrataLineage(
  seriesSlug: string,
  customRepoRoot?: string,
): ErrataLineageVerificationReport {
  const repoRoot = customRepoRoot || resolveRepoRoot()
  const ledgerPath = path.join(repoRoot, 'series', seriesSlug, 'world', 'errata.json')

  const errors: string[] = []
  const discontinuities: ErrataLineageVerificationReport['discontinuities'] = []

  if (!fs.existsSync(ledgerPath)) {
    return {
      valid: true,
      totalRecords: 0,
      genesisHash: '0'.repeat(64),
      headHash: '0'.repeat(64),
      errors: [],
      discontinuities: [],
    }
  }

  let ledger: ErrataLedgerFile
  try {
    ledger = loadErrataLedgerFile(ledgerPath)
  } catch (err: any) {
    return {
      valid: false,
      totalRecords: 0,
      genesisHash: '0'.repeat(64),
      headHash: '0'.repeat(64),
      errors: [`[MALFORMED_LEDGER_FILE] ${err.message}`],
      discontinuities: [],
    }
  }

  const records = ledger.records
  if (records.length === 0) {
    return {
      valid: true,
      totalRecords: 0,
      genesisHash: ledger.genesis_merkle_hash,
      headHash: ledger.genesis_merkle_hash,
      errors: [],
      discontinuities: [],
    }
  }

  let currentExpectedHash = ledger.genesis_merkle_hash

  for (let i = 0; i < records.length; i++) {
    const record = records[i]
    const expectedSeq = i + 1

    if (record.sequence_number !== expectedSeq) {
      errors.push(
        `[SEQUENCE_GAP] Expected sequence ${expectedSeq} at index ${i}, found ${record.sequence_number}`,
      )
    }

    if (record.superseded_merkle_hash !== currentExpectedHash) {
      errors.push(
        `[HASH_DISCONTINUITY] Sequence ${record.sequence_number} (${record.errata_id}) superseded hash ` +
          `'${record.superseded_merkle_hash.slice(0, 8)}...' does not match expected '${currentExpectedHash.slice(0, 8)}...'`,
      )
      discontinuities.push({
        sequenceNumber: record.sequence_number,
        errataId: record.errata_id,
        expectedSupersededHash: currentExpectedHash,
        actualSupersededHash: record.superseded_merkle_hash,
      })
    }

    currentExpectedHash = record.active_merkle_hash
  }

  return {
    valid: errors.length === 0,
    totalRecords: records.length,
    genesisHash: ledger.genesis_merkle_hash,
    headHash: currentExpectedHash,
    errors,
    discontinuities,
  }
}

export const appendErrataAction = (
  cpy: LawsModel,
  bal: ErrataOperationBit,
  ste?: State,
): LawsModel => {
  const dat = bal?.dat
  if (!dat || !dat.record) {
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        lawBit: {
          idx: 'append-errata-err',
          val: -1,
          dat: { success: false, error: '[MISSING_RECORD] record is required' },
        },
      })
    }
    return cpy
  }

  try {
    const res = appendErrataRecord(dat.seriesSlug, dat.record, dat.repoRoot)
    cpy.errataHistory.set(dat.record.errata_id, dat.record)
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        lawBit: {
          idx: 'append-errata',
          val: 0,
          dat: res,
        },
      })
    }
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        lawBit: {
          idx: 'append-errata-fail',
          val: -1,
          dat: { success: false, error: err.message },
        },
      })
    }
  }

  return cpy
}

export const verifyErrataAction = (
  cpy: LawsModel,
  bal: ErrataOperationBit,
  ste?: State,
): LawsModel => {
  const dat = bal?.dat
  const seriesSlug = dat?.seriesSlug || 'under-the-floorboards'
  const rep = verifyErrataLineage(seriesSlug, dat?.repoRoot)

  if (bal?.slv) {
    bal.slv({
      lawBit: {
        idx: 'verify-errata',
        val: rep.valid ? 0 : -1,
        dat: rep,
      },
    })
  }

  return cpy
}
```

#### 4. Update: `packages/299.lore/03.laws.unit/laws.reduce.ts`

```typescript
import clone from 'clone-deep'
import * as Act from './laws.action.js'
import { LawsModel } from './laws.model.js'
import * as Buzz from './laws.buzzer.js'
import type State from '../99.core/state.js'

export function reducer(
  model: LawsModel = new LawsModel(),
  act: Act.Actions,
  state?: State,
): LawsModel {
  switch (act.type) {
    case Act.INIT_LAWS:
      return Buzz.initLaws(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.UPDATE_LAWS:
      return Buzz.updateLaws(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.EVALUATE_PARDON_WAIVERS:
      return Buzz.evaluatePardonWaivers(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.APPEND_ERRATA:
      return Buzz.appendErrataAction(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.VERIFY_ERRATA:
      return Buzz.verifyErrataAction(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    default:
      return model
  }
}
```

```typescript
import type State from '../../99.core/state.js'
import type { MenuModel } from '../menu.model.js'
import type MenuBit from '../fce/menu.bit.js'
import { verifyErrataLineage } from '../../03.laws.unit/buz/errata.buzz.js'

const UPDATE_CONSOLE = '[Console action] Update Console'

async function emitConsole(ste: State | undefined, line: string): Promise<void> {
  const lib = (globalThis as any).LIBRARY || (global as any).LIBRARY
  if (lib && typeof lib.hunt === 'function') {
    await lib.hunt(UPDATE_CONSOLE, { idx: 'cns00', src: line }).catch(() => {})
  } else if (ste && typeof ste.hunt === 'function') {
    await ste.hunt(UPDATE_CONSOLE, { idx: 'cns00', src: line }).catch(() => {})
  }
}

export const runErrataMenu = async (
  cpy: MenuModel,
  bal: MenuBit,
  ste?: State,
): Promise<MenuModel> => {
  const seriesSlug = bal?.dat?.seriesSlug || cpy.activeSeries || 'under-the-floorboards'
  await emitConsole(ste, `>> [ERRATA:LINEAGE] Inspecting errata hash-chain for '${seriesSlug}'...`)

  const report = verifyErrataLineage(seriesSlug)

  if (report.valid) {
    const headShort = report.headHash.slice(0, 8)
    await emitConsole(
      ste,
      `>> [ERRATA:CHAIN_OK] Verified ${report.totalRecords} historical retcon(s) | Head: ${headShort}... Status: 0`,
    )
    cpy.statusMessage = 'ERRATA_CHAIN_VALID'
  } else {
    for (const err of report.errors) {
      await emitConsole(ste, `:: [ERRATA:DISCONTINUITY] ${err}`)
    }
    cpy.statusMessage = 'ERRATA_DISCONTINUITY'
  }

  if (bal?.slv) {
    bal.slv({
      mnuBit: {
        idx: 'run-errata-menu',
        val: report.valid ? 0 : -1,
        dat: report,
      },
    })
  }
  return cpy
}
```

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest'

describe('03.laws.unit :: Cryptographic Errata Lineage Sealer and Verifier', () => {
  let tempRepoRoot: string
  const seriesSlug = 'test-chronicle'
  const genesisHash = '0'.repeat(64)

  beforeEach(() => {

    const worldDir = path.join(tempRepoRoot, 'series', seriesSlug, 'world')
    fs.mkdirSync(worldDir, { recursive: true })
  })

  afterEach(() => {
    fs.rmSync(tempRepoRoot, { recursive: true, force: true })
  })

  it('appends the first errata record anchored to the genesis hash', () => {
    const record1: ErrataRecord = {
      errata_id: 'err_aperture_01',
      sequence_number: 1,
      classification: 'FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION',
      superseded_merkle_hash: genesisHash,
      active_merkle_hash: '1'.repeat(64),

      affected_entity_ids: ['loc_culvert_siphon'],

    const res = appendErrataRecord(seriesSlug, record1, tempRepoRoot)
    expect(res.success).toBe(true)
    expect(res.totalRecords).toBe(1)

    const ledger = loadErrataLedgerFile(res.ledgerPath!)
    expect(ledger.records.length).toBe(1)
    expect(ledger.records[0].errata_id).toBe('err_aperture_01')

    const audit = verifyErrataLineage(seriesSlug, tempRepoRoot)
    expect(audit.valid).toBe(true)
    expect(audit.totalRecords).toBe(1)
    expect(audit.headHash).toBe('1'.repeat(64))
  })

  it('appends multiple sequential records maintaining strict hash continuity', () => {
    const record1: ErrataRecord = {
      errata_id: 'err_seq_01',
      sequence_number: 1,
      classification: 'FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION',
      superseded_merkle_hash: genesisHash,
      active_merkle_hash: '1'.repeat(64),
      superseded_commit_sha: 'a'.repeat(40),
      active_commit_sha: 'b'.repeat(40),
      affected_entity_ids: ['loc_culvert_siphon'],
      historical_episodes: ['ep001'],

      active_merkle_hash: '2'.repeat(64),
      superseded_commit_sha: 'b'.repeat(40),
      active_commit_sha: 'c'.repeat(40),
      affected_entity_ids: ['char_wart'],

      rationale: 'Standardized left arm amputation date in timeline.',
      recorded_at_epoch: 200,

    appendErrataRecord(seriesSlug, record1, tempRepoRoot)
    const res2 = appendErrataRecord(seriesSlug, record2, tempRepoRoot)

    expect(res2.success).toBe(true)

    const audit = verifyErrataLineage(seriesSlug, tempRepoRoot)

    expect(audit.headHash).toBe('2'.repeat(64))

  it('rejects sequence number jumps or out-of-order appends', () => {

      active_commit_sha: 'b'.repeat(40),
      affected_entity_ids: ['loc_culvert_siphon'],
      historical_episodes: ['ep001'],
      rationale: 'First historical correction for pipe diameter.',
      recorded_at_epoch: 100,
    }
    appendErrataRecord(seriesSlug, record1, tempRepoRoot)

    // Artificially mutate errata.json on disk to simulate a broken chain
    const ledgerFile = path.join(tempRepoRoot, 'series', seriesSlug, 'world', 'errata.json')
    const ledger = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(ledgerFile, 'utf8'))
    ledger.records.push({
      errata_id: 'err_tampered_02',
      sequence_number: 2,
      classification: 'HISTORICAL_RETCON',
      superseded_merkle_hash: 'f'.repeat(64), // Does not match record1's active_merkle_hash
      active_merkle_hash: '9'.repeat(64),
      superseded_commit_sha: 'b'.repeat(40),
      active_commit_sha: 'c'.repeat(40),
      affected_entity_ids: ['char_bog'],
      historical_episodes: ['ep002'],
      rationale: 'Tampered hash continuity record.',

    fs.writeFileSync(ledgerFile, JSON.stringify(ledger, null, 2), 'utf8')

    const audit = verifyErrataLineage(seriesSlug, tempRepoRoot)
    expect(audit.valid).toBe(false)
    expect(audit.errors.some((e) => e.includes('[HASH_DISCONTINUITY]'))).toBe(true)
    expect(audit.discontinuities.length).toBe(1)
    expect(audit.discontinuities[0].errataId).toBe('err_tampered_02')
  })
})
```

### **FUNCTIONAL MANDATE**

#### **User Story**

In the quiet of the soundstage machine vault, four months after the premiere of *Under the Floorboards* Episode 101, an editorial emergency erupts across the narrative department. A guest director and the modeling lead are locking the layout for the season climax: a tense escape through the iron-bound culvert siphon. But an irreconcilable contradiction threatens production. In Episode 101, a brief line of background dialogue referred to the culvert siphon as six inches wide. However, the physical character rigs, weapon geometries, and tallow carrying packs designed in subsequent seasons physically require an eight-inch diameter aperture to allow bimanual passage.

In a conventional studio pipeline, this discrepancy triggers an unmitigated disaster: an editor silently opens the master lore database or the original script dossier, overwrites the word *six* with *eight*, and pushes the commit. That silent mutation instantly poisons the well: the original broadcast video manifests break, audio dialogue cache keys desynchronize, and nobody can verify whether an archival master is authentic or silently altered.

The lead continuity architect refuses to allow historical revisionism to corrupt mathematical reality. In `000.goblin-lore`, history is immutable. The original broadcast release of Episode 101 must remain forever bit-identical and verifiable against its historical Merkle root. Instead of overwriting history, the architect opens the Blessed terminal flight deck and triggers the **Cryptographic Errata Lineage Sealer**.

The architect enters an official retcon: `err_culvert_aperture_01`, classified under `FACTUAL_CONTRADICTION`, sequence number 1. The engine verifies that this entry supersedes the exact genesis Merkle root ($H_{\text{genesis}}$), calculates the new active Merkle hash ($H_{\text{active}}$), binds the active Git commit SHA, and atomically commits the record into `series/under-the-floorboards/world/errata.json` using a sibling temporary file swap. When future compilation runs occur, the three-pass compiler traces this unbroken hash chain: the historical broadcast stands verified in amber, while the live master advances forward through a tamper-evident, cryptographically audited lineage of truth.

#### **Strategic Goal**

Supports the primary project objective of **Non-Repudiable Cryptographic Lineage & Zero-Drift Historical Preservation ($T_0 = \$0.00$)**. By enforcing an append-only, cryptographically linked hash chain on post-broadcast narrative corrections and retcons, this task guarantees that prior episodes remain verifiable against their original broadcast Merkle seals while current and future episodes compile against a mathematically audited chain of custody without silent mutations or retcon drift.

- **The Strategic Value:** Resolves the fundamental tension between creative narrative evolution and immutable content-addressed storage. Eliminates silent file overwrites, unrecorded retcons, and broken media cache keys across multi-season transmedia franchises by proving that every change in canonical world state is chained forward via SHA-256 cryptographic continuity.
- **The Technical Challenge:** Constructing a deterministic append-only state engine that enforces strict monotonic sequence numbering ($1, 2, \dots, N$), prevents cyclic or self-referential hash loops ($H_{\text{superseded}} \neq H_{\text{active}}$), guarantees atomic POSIX write safety via `.tmp_[UUID]` renames, and traverses the hash chain in memory to expose structured failure reports on sequence gaps or hash discontinuities without touching the immutable harness boundary in `apps/995.library/`.

#### 1. Create: `packages/299.lore/41.canon.unit/fce/standing.schema.ts`

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod'

export const EpistemologicalStandingEnum = z.enum([
  'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
  'FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW',
  'DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED',
])
export type EpistemologicalStanding = z.infer<typeof EpistemologicalStandingEnum>

export const VALID_EPISTEMOLOGICAL_STANDINGS: readonly EpistemologicalStanding[] = Object.freeze([
  'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
  'FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW',
  'DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED',
] as const)

export function isEpistemologicalStanding(value: unknown): value is EpistemologicalStanding {
  return typeof value === 'string' && VALID_EPISTEMOLOGICAL_STANDINGS.includes(value as EpistemologicalStanding)
}

export interface StandingMetadata {
  standing: EpistemologicalStanding
  badge: 'GREEN' | 'YELLOW' | 'RED'
  cascadeOnEnter: boolean
  compileEnforced: boolean
}

export const STANDING_METADATA_REGISTRY: Readonly<Record<EpistemologicalStanding, StandingMetadata>> = Object.freeze({
  ACTIVE_ENDORSED: Object.freeze({
    standing: 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
    badge: 'GREEN',
    cascadeOnEnter: false,
    compileEnforced: true,
  }),
  FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW: Object.freeze({
    standing: 'FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW',
    badge: 'YELLOW',
    cascadeOnEnter: false,
    compileEnforced: true,
  }),
  DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED: Object.freeze({
    standing: 'DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED',
    badge: 'RED',
    cascadeOnEnter: true,
    compileEnforced: false,
  }),
})

export function getStandingMetadata(standing: EpistemologicalStanding): StandingMetadata {
  return STANDING_METADATA_REGISTRY[standing]
}

export const CanonFactStandingSchema = z
  .object({
    fact_id: z.string().regex(/^fact_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[STANDING_SCHEMA_BREACH] fact_id must match pattern ^fact_[a-z0-9_]+$',
    }),
    entity_id: z.string().regex(/^[a-z]+_[a-z0-9_]+$/, {
      message: '[STANDING_SCHEMA_BREACH] entity_id must match standard entity identifier',
    }),
    standing: EpistemologicalStandingEnum,
    in_degree_count: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] in_degree_count must be an integer' })
      .min(0, { message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] in_degree_count cannot be negative' }),
    days_since_reconsideration: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] days_since_reconsideration must be an integer' })
      .min(0, { message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] days_since_reconsideration cannot be negative' }),
    last_reviewed_epoch: z
      .number()
      .int({ message: '[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] last_reviewed_epoch must be an integer' })
      .nonnegative({ message: '[OUT_OF_BOUNDS] last_reviewed_epoch cannot be negative' })
      .default(0),
    review_note: z.string().min(5).optional(),
  })
  .strict()

export type CanonFactStanding = z.infer<typeof CanonFactStandingSchema>
```

```typescript
import {

export const inspectEpistemicStandingRegistryAction = async (
  cpy: MenuModel,
  bal: MenuBit,
  ste?: State,
): Promise<MenuModel> => {
  await emitConsoleLine(ste, '>> [STANDING:INSPECT] Validating Epistemic Standing Registry...')
```

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
import {
  EpistemologicalStandingEnum,
  VALID_EPISTEMOLOGICAL_STANDINGS,
  isEpistemologicalStanding,
  getStandingMetadata,
  CanonFactStandingSchema,
  type CanonFactStanding,
} from '../fce/standing.schema.js'

describe('41.canon.unit :: Tri-State Epistemological Standing Schema Contract', () => {
  const validStandingRecord: CanonFactStanding = {
    fact_id: 'fact_wart_arm_amputation',
    entity_id: 'char_wart',
    standing: 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
    in_degree_count: 12,
    days_since_reconsideration: 30,
    last_reviewed_epoch: 100,
    review_note: 'Baseline physical amputation fact affirmed at season start.',
  }

  it('validates a compliant CanonFactStanding record', () => {
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(validStandingRecord)
    expect(result.success).toBe(true)
  })

  it('verifies metadata definitions for all 3 epistemological states', () => {
    expect(VALID_EPISTEMOLOGICAL_STANDINGS).toHaveLength(3)

    const activeMeta = getStandingMetadata('ACTIVE_ENDORSED')
    expect(activeMeta.badge).toBe('GREEN')
    expect(activeMeta.cascadeOnEnter).toBe(false)
    expect(activeMeta.compileEnforced).toBe(true)

    const flaggedMeta = getStandingMetadata('FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW')
    expect(flaggedMeta.badge).toBe('YELLOW')
    expect(flaggedMeta.cascadeOnEnter).toBe(false)
    expect(flaggedMeta.compileEnforced).toBe(true)

    const deprecatedMeta = getStandingMetadata('DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED')
    expect(deprecatedMeta.badge).toBe('RED')
    expect(deprecatedMeta.cascadeOnEnter).toBe(true)
    expect(deprecatedMeta.compileEnforced).toBe(false)
  })

  it('validates type guard isEpistemologicalStanding', () => {
    expect(isEpistemologicalStanding('ACTIVE_ENDORSED')).toBe(true)
    expect(isEpistemologicalStanding('FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW')).toBe(true)
    expect(isEpistemologicalStanding('DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED')).toBe(true)
    expect(isEpistemologicalStanding('UNKNOWN_STATE')).toBe(false)
    expect(isEpistemologicalStanding(null)).toBe(false)
  })

  it('rejects floating-point numbers in in_degree_count', () => {
    const floatInDegree = {
      ...validStandingRecord,
      in_degree_count: 12.5,
    }
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(floatInDegree)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects floating-point numbers in days_since_reconsideration', () => {
    const floatDays = {
      ...validStandingRecord,
      days_since_reconsideration: 1.2,
    }
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(floatDays)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects floating-point numbers in last_reviewed_epoch', () => {
    const floatEpoch = {
      ...validStandingRecord,
      last_reviewed_epoch: 100.75,
    }
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(floatEpoch)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects negative integer counts', () => {
    const negativeCount = {
      ...validStandingRecord,
      in_degree_count: -1,
    }
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(negativeCount)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[OUT_OF_BOUNDS]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects malformed fact_id identifiers', () => {
    const badId = {
      ...validStandingRecord,
      fact_id: 'invalid_prefix_arm',
    }
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(badId)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
    if (!result.success) {
      expect(result.error.issues[0].message).toContain('[STANDING_SCHEMA_BREACH]')
    }
  })

  it('rejects undeclared properties in strict mode', () => {
    const rogueKeys = {
      ...validStandingRecord,
      unauthorized_mutation: true,
    }
    const result = CanonFactStandingSchema.safeParse(rogueKeys)
    expect(result.success).toBe(false)
  })
})
```

### **FUNCTIONAL MANDATE**

#### **User Story**

Elena sat alone in the writer's room cockpit during the twilight hours of Episode 104, staring at the dependency DAG glowing across her terminal. Two hours prior, a storyboard artist had noticed an offhand line of dialogue recorded in the pilot: Wart had casually remarked that the culvert siphon hatch was secured with double iron deadbolts. Now, three episodes later, the climax required Bog to shatter that hatch with a single blow from an eight-pound miner's sledge.

In earlier pipeline iterations, challenging an authored fact felt like pulling a grenade pin. Simply editing the dossier or marking a ticket would flip the fact to invalid, triggering an unbuffered cascade. Hundreds of downstream scenes, vocal stems, and layout plates would be flagged dirty, freezing the cloud GPU render farm and burning thousands of dollars in wasted compute. Writers had grown silent, terrified of questioning canon because questioning canon broke the studio's active build.

With the **Tri-State Epistemological Standing Schema** active in `41.canon.unit`, Elena exhaled. She pulled up `fact_wart_culvert_deadbolt` and shifted its status from `ACTIVE_ENDORSED` to `FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW`.

Instantly, the system engaged the **Liminal State Zero-Cascade Guarantee**. An amber advisory badge illuminated in the Director Console, but zero `is_dirty` flags fired across downstream scenes. Active rendering workers on the soundstage hummed uninterrupted, preserving every micro-dollar of budget. The creative team had gained a safe, cost-free room to debate, test, and deliberate without holding the production pipeline hostage to artistic doubt.

#### **Strategic Goal**

Supports the primary project objective of **Zero-Cascade Epistemological Deliberation ($T_0 = \$0.00$) and Non-Destructive Canon Scrutiny**. By establishing an explicit three-stage lifecycle (`ACTIVE_ENDORSED`, `FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW`, `DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED`), the system decouples creative doubt from automated build halts, guaranteeing that only ratified retcons trigger downstream invalidation cascades.

#### **Context & Value**

- **The Strategic Value:** Solves Epistemological Calcification—the systemic failure where writers become trapped by casual lines authored early in a series because questioning them breaks the production build. It provides an immutable, liminal buffer state where facts can be flagged and scrutinized without incurring immediate financial, rendering, or scheduling penalties.
- **The Technical Challenge:** Enforcing closed lifecycle transitions in TypeScript and Zod while strictly regulating cascade side-effects, guaranteeing integer metric purity across in-degree counts and days without review, rejecting floating-point decimal drift, and integrating typed `Map` stores into `CanonModel` without violating the immutable runner boundary in `apps/995.library/`.

#### **Interface**

- **`000.goblin-lore` (`packages/299.lore` / `41.canon.unit`):** Primary workspace and home unit hosting the standing schemas, types, standing metadata definitions, and in-memory `factStandings` registry within `CanonModel`.
- **`26.schema.unit` (`packages/299.lore`):** Ingests standing definitions to validate candidate frontmatter against closed lifecycle bounds.
- **`002.worker-sower` (`worker-sower-engine`):** Evaluates `cascadeOnEnter` during state delta commits to ensure only `DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED` transitions trigger `is_dirty = 1` scene sweeps.
- **`apps/995.library` (`@camp_candor/995.library`):** Blessed terminal host that mounts the standing registry inspection action via `run.ts` while enforcing strict boundary immutability (0 dirty lines).

#### **Interaction**

- **Blessed Terminal Cockpit (`packages/299.lore/98.menu.unit`):**
  - Accessed through the terminal runner: `npm run dev` (launching `apps/995.library/run.ts -t lore`).
  - Navigated via `LORE MENU` (`globalKey: "LORE"`), opening `[CANON MENU] -> [1] INSPECT EPISTEMIC STANDING REGISTRY`.
  - Synchronously triggers `inspectEpistemicStandingRegistryAction` in `98.menu.unit/buz/00.menu.buzz.ts`, validating sample fact candidates against `CanonFactStandingSchema` and streaming real-time 7-bit ASCII receipts into console pane `cns00` (`{ x: 4, y: 0, xSpan: 8, ySpan: 12 }`):
    ```plaintext
    >> [STANDING:INSPECT] Validating Epistemic Standing Registry...
    >> [STANDING:SCHEMA_OK] fact_wart_arm_amputation validated | Badge: YELLOW | CascadeOnEnter: false
    ```
  - In the presence of a malformed identifier or floating-point input, the console instantly emits:
    ```plaintext
    :: [STANDING:SCHEMA_FAIL] [FLOAT_PROHIBITED] in_degree_count must be an integer
    ```

#### 2. Create: `packages/299.lore/41.canon.unit/buz/standing.buzz.ts`

```typescript
import type { CanonFactStanding } from '../fce/standing.schema.js'
import type {
  ReconsiderationPriorityRecord,
  StillGoodAffirmationResult,
  default as CanonReconsiderationBit,
} from '../fce/reconsideration.bit.js'
import type { CanonModel } from '../canon.model.js'
import type State from '../../99.core/state.js'

/**
 * Calculates topological blast-radius review priority score in integer basis points.
 * Score = DaysSinceReconsideration * log10(DependentScenes + 1) * 100
 * Bounded to discrete integers to eliminate IEEE 754 float drift.
 */
export function calculateAuditPriorityScoreBps(
  daysSinceReconsideration: number,
  downstreamDependentScenes: number,
): number {
  if (!Number.isInteger(daysSinceReconsideration)) {
    throw new Error('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] daysSinceReconsideration must be an integer')
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(downstreamDependentScenes)) {
    throw new Error('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] downstreamDependentScenes must be an integer')
  }
  if (daysSinceReconsideration <= 0) return 0
  if (downstreamDependentScenes < 0) return 0

  const rawScore = daysSinceReconsideration * Math.log10(downstreamDependentScenes + 1)
  return Math.round(rawScore * 100)
}

/**
 * Evaluates all tracked facts and returns an ordered queue of audit candidates.
 */
export function rankReconsiderationQueue(
  factCatalog: Map<string, CanonFactStanding> | Record<string, CanonFactStanding>,
  currentEpoch: number = 0,
  minDaysStale: number = 0,
): ReconsiderationPriorityRecord[] {
  if (!Number.isInteger(currentEpoch)) {
    throw new Error('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] currentEpoch must be an integer')
  }

  const factList = factCatalog instanceof Map ? Array.from(factCatalog.values()) : Object.values(factCatalog)
  const candidates: ReconsiderationPriorityRecord[] = []
  const secondsPerDay = 86400

  for (const fact of factList) {
    if (fact.standing === 'DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED') continue

    const elapsedSeconds = Math.max(0, currentEpoch - fact.last_reviewed_epoch)
    const daysStale = Math.max(fact.days_since_reconsideration, Math.floor(elapsedSeconds / secondsPerDay))

    if (daysStale >= minDaysStale || fact.standing === 'FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW') {
      const scoreBps = calculateAuditPriorityScoreBps(daysStale, fact.in_degree_count)
      const isMonolithicSpine = fact.in_degree_count >= 12 && daysStale > 60

      candidates.push({
        fact_id: fact.fact_id,
        entity_id: fact.entity_id,
        standing: fact.standing,
        in_degree_count: fact.in_degree_count,
        days_since_reconsideration: daysStale,
        priority_score_bps: scoreBps,
        is_monolithic_spine: isMonolithicSpine,
      })
    }
  }

  return candidates.sort((a, b) => {
    if (b.priority_score_bps !== a.priority_score_bps) {
      return b.priority_score_bps - a.priority_score_bps
    }
    return a.fact_id.localeCompare(b.fact_id)
  })
}

/**
 * Executes the 5-second "Still Good" re-affirmation protocol.
 * Resets stale duration, preserves version, and triggers zero cascades.
 */
export function affirmStillGood(
  factCatalog: Map<string, CanonFactStanding>,
  factId: string,
  affirmationEpoch: number = 0,
): StillGoodAffirmationResult {
  if (!Number.isInteger(affirmationEpoch)) {
    throw new Error('[FLOAT_PROHIBITED] affirmationEpoch must be an integer')
  }

  const existing = factCatalog.get(factId)
  if (!existing) {
    throw new Error(`[FACT_NOT_FOUND] Cannot affirm non-existent fact '${factId}'`)
  }

  const previousStanding = existing.standing
  existing.last_reviewed_epoch = affirmationEpoch
  existing.days_since_reconsideration = 0

  if (existing.standing === 'FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW') {
    existing.standing = 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED'
  }

  return {
    success: true,
    fact_id: factId,
    version_bumped: false,
    cascade_triggered: false,
    updated_last_reviewed_epoch: affirmationEpoch,
    previous_standing: previousStanding,
    current_standing: existing.standing,
  }
}

export const rankReconsiderationQueueAction = (
  cpy: CanonModel,
  bal: CanonReconsiderationBit,
  ste?: State,
): CanonModel => {
  const dat = bal?.dat
  const currentEpoch = dat?.currentEpoch ?? 0
  const minDaysStale = dat?.minDaysStale ?? 0

  const queue = rankReconsiderationQueue(cpy.factStandings, currentEpoch, minDaysStale)

  if (bal?.slv) {
    bal.slv({
      canBit: {
        idx: 'rank-reconsideration-queue',
        val: 0,
        dat: queue,
      },
    })
  }
  return cpy
}

export const affirmStillGoodAction = (
  cpy: CanonModel,
  bal: CanonReconsiderationBit,
  ste?: State,
): CanonModel => {
  const dat = bal?.dat
  if (!dat || !dat.factId) {
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        canBit: {
          idx: 'affirm-still-good-err',
          val: -1,
          dat: {
            success: false,
            fact_id: '',
            version_bumped: false,
            cascade_triggered: false,
            updated_last_reviewed_epoch: 0,
            previous_standing: 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
            current_standing: 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
          },
        },
      })
    }
    return cpy
  }

  try {
    const res = affirmStillGood(cpy.factStandings, dat.factId, dat.currentEpoch ?? 0)
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        canBit: {
          idx: 'affirm-still-good',
          val: 0,
          dat: res,
        },
      })
    }
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (bal?.slv) {
      bal.slv({
        canBit: {
          idx: 'affirm-still-good-fail',
          val: -1,
          dat: {
            success: false,
            fact_id: dat.factId,
            version_bumped: false,
            cascade_triggered: false,
            updated_last_reviewed_epoch: 0,
            previous_standing: 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
            current_standing: 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',
          },
        },
      })
    }
  }
  return cpy
}
```

```typescript
import type { Action } from '../99.core/interface/action.interface.js'
import type CanonBit from './fce/canon.bit.js'
```

```typescript
import clone from 'clone-deep'
import * as Act from './canon.action.js'
import { CanonModel } from './canon.model.js'
import * as Buzz from './canon.buzzer.js'
import type State from '../99.core/state.js'

export function reducer(
  model: CanonModel = new CanonModel(),
  act: Act.Actions,
  state?: State,
): CanonModel {
  switch (act.type) {
    case Act.INIT_CANON:
      return Buzz.initCanon(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.UPDATE_CANON:
      return Buzz.updateCanon(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.RANK_RECONSIDERATION_QUEUE:
      return Buzz.rankReconsiderationQueueAction(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    case Act.AFFIRM_STILL_GOOD:
      return Buzz.affirmStillGoodAction(clone(model), act.bale, state)

    default:
      return model
  }
}
```
